content_metadata.description: An in-depth look into the character Azazel from the Total War series, exploring his lore, gameplay mechanics, sound design, and animation, alongside insights into the development of War Shrines for each Chaos god.

qAndA.answer: Azazel can easily upgrade Undivided champions, essentially tempting them with power in exchange for serving Slaanesh.
qAndA.question: How is Azazel's 'deal with the devil' theme reflected in his gameplay mechanics?

qAndA.answer: Azazel is a flying lord, granting him greater mobility and strategic advantage on the battlefield, which is a first for Slaanesh.
qAndA.question: What makes Azazel a unique choice for playing as Slaanesh compared to other lords?

qAndA.answer: Azazel’s sound design incorporates synthetic heartbeats and pulses alongside organic textures, creating a distinctively 'Slaaneshi' feel that is both alluring and unsettling.
qAndA.question: What are some of the unsettling sonic elements used in Azazel's sound design?

qAndA.answer: Each War Shrine has bespoke sound effects: Undivided features chaotic lightning, Khorne has aggressive, distorted fire, Tzeentch has Doppler effects highlighting speed, and Nurgle’s sounds were not described in detail.
qAndA.question: How does the sound design of the War Shrines reflect the nature of each Chaos god?

qAndA.answer: Azazel’s animations are designed to showcase his vanity and desire to show off his speed and prowess as a warrior. He moves with flair and emphasizes his deadly elegance when killing enemies.
qAndA.question: What is the primary focus of Azazel’s animations on the battlefield?

text_to_speech: Azazel is kind of a fun one because in a lot of ways he is basically Lucifer, right? He's the fallen angel. He's got the feathery wings, he's got the alliance with the God of man, and all that So he's a kind of fun character to play around with in that respect And a big part of that is the idea of temptation The deal with the devil, right? We kind of touched on some aspects of that in the N'Kari campaign with some of the features like, you know, seducing units and sort of influence. And we kind of want to bring that across to Azazel, but we also wanted to explore how that works within the context of Chaos. So he's covering up these undivided champions and he's saying, "Well, if you serve Slaanesh rather than Khorne or Nurgle this is what you get, this is the kind of gifts I'm offering you." So in gameplay terms of the four champions, he's the one who leans most into our Path to Glory system, which is about the character progression, about upgrading the characters. So you'll find it a bit cheaper to create his characters, you'll find it easier to upgrade these characters and to kind of lean into this idea that he's almost like a mentor figure to this next generation of Slaaneshi champions. Azazel is really flexible. He's a really good pick for Slaanesh because he can fly. Previously, they didn't have a flying Lord. He is a bit of a can opener. He's got this kind of armour piercing quality to him. He's also very, very good at casting. He's a Lore of Slaanesh caster, so he's great for just dropping really powerful AOE spells, like slicing shards on your enemies. What's really cool about this project was obviously the four Champions of Chaos and we had four sound designers, so we all took one each and all kind of made it our own and worked together as a team and went back and forward. So it was my good friend Alex Hynes who did Azazel. And I think one of the key things we talked about when talking about Azazel and how Azazel should sound is, it just needed to be very Slaanesh. So all of Azazel's sounds have this really organic texture to it. There's a bit synthetic so it sounds a bit off, but it's a nice hybrid. So again, it feels like Slaanesh So like a lot of his abilities have these like pulses that happen and they're like almost like synthetic heartbeats. So they feel right but wrong. And of course, our animators and VFX department did a phenomenal job. So it made it really easy for Alex to make all the sound design for all of his Azazel's melee that's probably his big thing. And because Azazel is a quick character, all his attacks are very quick and to the point, and there's a lot of kick-drums and a lot of his impacts, and it's just there to give him a nice like [punch sound effect] Straight to the point. For Azazel, we were mostly trying to adapt the lore into the animation. He likes himself, from his point of view, he's the most beautiful thing in the earth. He's trying to show off while he kills people His speed and his skill are his best assets on the battlefield. And that's what we showed in his animation. The War Shrines; they're all bespoke war shrines to each god. And I think it would've been very easy to give them all of the same sounds and just leave it there. And it's, you know, giant chaos monsters carrying giant metal shrines, essentially. So them sounds were the same, but what we've done differently is just these big VFX that are playing off them and they are all very bespoke to them gods. When you play as Undivided this is really Chaos Lightning type thing. When you play Khorne it's got this really aggressive fire. Super distorted, really over the top, really  Khorne And the Slaanesh one was really cool because we gave it a lot of, the audio in the mix, we gave it a lot of Doppler effect. So as the little VFX are whoosing by you're getting it because again, Slaanesh is speed, so we like the idea that the shrine sound effects have, for Slaanesh, have these like [whoosing noises] constantly playing, because it's Slaanesh.
